newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers offer Clinton school repair bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers offer Clinton school repair bill.

text.p: U.S. Representative Nita Lowey and Senator Carol Mosely-Braun on Tuesday introduced President Clinton's $5 billion school construction bill, but the measure faces an uphill battle on Capitol Hill, congressional aides said.

The bill, which the White House sent to Capitol Hill on March 14, would allocate $5 billion in federal funds nationwide to offset up to 50 percent of the cost of financing new school construction or renovation.
About $245 billion would go directly to 100 large school districts nationwide. Another $2.45 billion would be distributed to the 50 states.

"This is a local problem that deserves a national response," Lowey, a New York Democrat, said in a written statement. "We simply cannot prepare America's children for the 21st century in 19th century schools."

Part of the bill's funding could go to wiring school computer labs with up-to-date technology. "We can't train the workers of the future with the equipment of the past," said Rep. Joseph Kennedy, D-Mass., a cosponsor of the Lowey bill.
Moseley-Braun, D-Ill., said Illinois school districts would get an estimated $201.7 million under the bill, including $117 million for Chicago schools.

But an aide to Rep. William Goodling, R-Pa., chairman of the House Economic and Educational Opportunities Committee, said her boss questions whether school renovation is the federal government's proper role, whether the bill improperly rewards school districts that haven't managed funds properly, and whether it will drive up the U.S. deficit.
